source_text: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) 2012 policy, based on systematic review of studies, found benefits—including reduced urinary tract infections (by 90% in first year), penile cancer, and heterosexual HIV/STI acquisition—outweigh rare complications (0.2-0.6% rate, mostly minor bleeding or infection), justifying access but deferring to parental decision without routine endorsement due to non-universal applicability. [126] [108]
